- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes unrealistically; increase early forecast values, especially if sentiment dips sharply.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00) by overshooting 20–40% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to forecast peaks.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat (0.00–0.33), model often underperforms; adjust forecast upward by 5–15% for first 5–7 days of horizon.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 10–20% in next 3–5 days; if below, increase by 5–10%.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven “late-cycle” corrections (e.g., sentiment = 1.00 → price drops 15–30% in final 7–10 days); add 1–2% downward adjustment in last 7 days if sentiment was high.
- If sentiment history shows “reversal” (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00), model often misses the drop; reduce forecast by 10–25% in final 5–7 days.
